Apply them to an organizational situation, and analyze their advantages and drawbacks. 3.Read the case and answer the following. Anita Sharma is the head of the marketing department in a mid-sized firm. She maintains close working relationships with a few team members who regularly communicate with her take on additional responsibilities, and are trusted with important assignments. These employees receive more feedback, flexibility, and development opportunities. Other team members, however, have limited interaction with Anita and are assigned routine tasks with little autonomy. Over time, differences in access to information and opportunities become noticeable within the team. While the high-trust group shows strong commitment and performance, the rest of the team feels disengaged and less motivated. This uneven relationship pattern affects collaboration, perceptions of fairness, and overall team effectiveness. 1.Identify the leadership theory that best describes Anita Sharma’s style and explain it in relation to this case. 2.Evaluate the problems created by this style and suggest solutions to enhance fairness and team collaboration.

subject: Introduction to Organizational Psychology
text: Explain Kurt Lewin’s Three-Step Model of Change. Illustrate its application in the context of a college, and analyze its effectiveness in managing change in educational institutions. 3.Read the case and answer the following. A senior committee in a reputed engineering college is formed to decide on the rapid expansion of online programs. The committee is led by a highly respected chairperson whose opinions dominate discussions. Meetings are brief and marked by quick agreement. Members avoid raising objections to maintain harmony and avoid appearing negative. Those who express doubts about faculty workload, infrastructure readiness, or quality standards are subtly pressured to align with the majority view. The committee assumes that unanimous agreement indicates a correct decision and does not seek external opinions. As a result, the program is launched without adequate planning. Within a year, the college faces declining academic quality, faculty dissatisfaction, and student complaints. 1.Identify and explain the major problem with the committee’s process and evaluate its impact on program quality and stakeholder satisfaction. 2.Evaluate the decision-making failures and suggest measures to improve planning participation, and decision quality in the committee.
